newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH FIRST DIVISION.

text.p: Matches to be played in the Spanish first division this weekend:
(league position in paretheses; all kickoff times gmt)
Saturday
Sevilla (20) v Valencia (15) 1930 gmt
Both sides are desperate for points, and Sevilla are yet to
win at home. Valencia's Romario will be hoping to make
amends for sleeping through much of Thursday's training
session.
Compostela (18) v Barcelona (2) 1830
Barcelona are still not playing well as a team, but led by
brilliant BraziLian striker Ronaldo they should have enough
individual talent to overcome last year's surprise outfit.
Tenerife (6) v Valladolid (11) 1700
Tenerife have won two home games 6-0, but have suspension and
injury problems in defence while striker Jose Quevedo is
back for Valladolid, who normally do well in the Canaries.
Zaragoza (19) V Athletic Bilbao (17) 1830
Zaragoza fans will greet the referee with 15,000 whistles in
a match that will be played in the shadow of a hotly-disputed
penalty in the last home game against Barcelona.
Espanyol (14) v Celta Vigo (16) 1600
Celta will be hoping that lightning-quick forward Miguel
Angel Benitez won't make it back from Wednesday's match for
Paraguay in time to lead the Espanyol attack.
Atletico Madrid (7) v Real Betis (3) 1800
Champions Atletico will miss injured playmaker Jose Luis
Caminero in the big game of the weekend against a Betis
side with striker Alfonso Perez in devastating form.
Sunday
Oviedo (10) v Deportivo Coruna (4) 1500
John Toshack's Deportivo are at their best away from home
and will start as favourites despite losing midfielder
Rafael Martin Vazquez through injury.
Rayo Vallecano (13) v Hercules (21) 1500
Rayo have won their last two home games 3-0, and with
Brazilian striker Guilherme in fine form should have no
trouble against newly-promoted Hercules, who are yet to
score away.
Real Sociedad (5) v Extremadura (22) 1500
Real Sociedad have Serbian midfielder Darko Kovacevic back
from World Cup duty and should have no problems against
new boys Extremadura, who have lost all six matches.
Racing Santander (9) v Real Madrid (1) 1730
Leaders Real have nine players back from midweek World Cup
games to visit a side that traditionally gives problems to
Spain's bigger teams and may threaten their unbeaten record.
Logrones (8) v Sporting Gijon (12) 1500
Newly-promoted Logrones have started strongly, but will be
without veteran goalkeeper Andoni Cedrun for the game
against a side that tends to play best away from home.
